t.7.53.1: As the sages were speaking thus, Kākutstha spoke these words: "Tell me, what is it that you need done? I will destroy your fear."
t.7.53.2: When Kākutstha had spoken thus, Bhārgava said these words: "Hear, O lord of men, what is the root of the fear that besets us and the land."
t.7.53.3: Long ago, in the Kṛta Yuga, O Rāma, there was a Daitya of exceedingly great strength, the eldest son of Lolā, a mighty Asura named Madhu.
t.7.53.4: He was devoted to the brahmins, a refuge to those who sought shelter, and firmly grounded in wisdom; and he enjoyed an incomparable friendship with the supremely noble gods.
t.7.53.5: That Madhu was endowed with valour and firmly devoted to dharma, and out of great esteem Rudra granted him a wondrous boon.
t.7.53.6: Drawing forth from his own trident a trident of great power and great splendour, the great-souled one, well pleased, gave it and spoke these words.
t.7.53.7: By you this incomparable and auspicious righteousness has been accomplished through my grace. Filled with supreme delight, I give you an excellent weapon.
t.7.53.8: As long as you do not oppose the gods and the brahmins, O great asura, so long shall this trident be yours; otherwise it would meet its destruction.
t.7.53.9: Whoever, free from fear, should attack you for battle, him the trident will reduce to ashes and then return again to your hand.
t.7.53.10: Having thus obtained the boon from Rudra, the great asura bowed down once more to Mahādeva and spoke these words.
t.7.53.11: O Lord, may this unsurpassed trident remain forever with my lineage, O god, for you are indeed the lord of the gods.
t.7.53.12: To Madhu, as he spoke thus, the god Śiva, lord of all beings, the great god Mahādeva, replied: "This shall not come to pass in this way."
t.7.53.14: As long as this trident remains in the hand of your son, he will be unslayable by all beings, so long as he holds the trident in his hand.
t.7.53.13: May your auspicious words, spoken through my grace, not be in vain; but this trident shall pass to one son of yours alone.
t.7.53.15: Having thus obtained the boon from the god, Madhu, the foremost of the Asuras, had a very great, wondrous and radiant palace built.
t.7.53.17: Her son, of great prowess, was the fierce Lavaṇa by name. Wicked-souled from childhood onward, he committed nothing but evil deeds.
t.7.53.16: His wife was the illustrious and beloved Kumbhīnasī, the child of the Viśvāsa couple, born of Analā and possessed of great radiance.
t.7.53.18: Seeing that ill-behaved son, Madhu, filled with distress, fell into grief, and he said nothing at all to him.
t.7.53.20: Through the power of his spear and through his own wickedness, he torments the three worlds, but the ascetics above all.
t.7.53.19: Having placed the trident in the keeping of Lavaṇa, he made known the boon to him; then, leaving this world, he entered the abode of Varuṇa.
t.7.53.21: Such is the might of Lavaṇa, and such too is his spear; having heard what the measure of it is, decide, O Kākutstha, for you indeed are our supreme refuge.
t.7.53.22: O Rāma, many kings were in the past entreated for protection by the sages tormented by fear, yet, O hero, we know of no protector.
t.7.53.23: Having heard that Rāvaṇa was slain together with his army and mounts, we know of no other protector on earth, O Rāma, no other lord of men. Therefore, tormented by fear, we wish to be rescued from Lavaṇa.
